analysis:
The PR touches only tests and benchmark tooling. It adds no production source, so no new attack surface or invalidated trust assumption was found.

1. LaunchAgentRestartTests.swift (head lines 181-203) adds forwardsPrefillGeometryRollbackToProviderJob. It asserts that EngineV2Factory.prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey pass through LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment into the service plist, while UNRELATED_SECRET is excluded. It also asserts that WatchdogAgent.passthroughEnvKeys does not include these keys. The test therefore reinforces the env allowlist, which keeps non-allowlisted secrets out of the plist. The behaviour that allowlists these two keys lives in production code outside this diff (LaunchAgent.inferencePassthroughEnvKeys) and was not supplied. The keys are performance tuning knobs for prefill chunk size and step token budget. The allowlist and operator-controlled env are local-operator surfaces; T-041/TB-007 concerns around prefix-cache behaviour and chunking are not obviously affected, though the real geometry change cannot be verified from these files. The concern in TB-003, that the operator already has full local control, is unchanged.

2. config.py (head lines 33-37) is a comment-only change documenting a benchmark schema note. validation.py (line 16) adds scheduler prefill raw schema version 5 to the accepted set. This widens a benchmark validator's accepted versions in a developer script and does not affect provider runtime, attestation, or any asset in the threat model.

Remaining question for integration: the production Swift changes that introduce prefillGeometry, prefillChunkKey and stepTokenBudgetKey, and the Gemma 2048/4096 defaults, are not in this batch. They should be reviewed there for memory or availability effects (T-029, T-041) and for env-var handling, given that DARKBLOOM_* knobs are forwarded into launchd.
